summary.value: The Silverudd Blue is a Swedish chicken created by Martin Silverudd in the Småland region of southern Sweden. He started mainly from New Hampshire and Rhode Island Red birds and crossed in Cream Legbars from Britain to get colored eggshells. Hens lay blue to green eggs of roughly 50 to 65 grams. Silverudd died in 1986 before the work was finished, so birds today still differ in size and in egg shade. The breed went by names such as Isbar and Swedish green egg layer before it took its creator's name in 2016. It is a medium-sized bird with a square outline, a single comb, four toes, dark legs and a dark beak. Hens weigh about 3.3 pounds and roosters about 5.5 pounds. Because it carries the blue gene, chicks hatch in black, blue or splash in a steady ratio, with blue the most common.
